children: Taiwan's inflation remained elevated in August, strengthening the case for an interest-rate increase ahead of the central bank's meeting next week.
The consumer-price index rose 2.04% from a year earlier, missing the 2.4% increase expected by economists polled by The Wall Street Journal.
The reading marked the fourth consecutive month that inflation exceeded 2%, as the Middle East conflict drove up energy costs while typhoons and heavy summer rains lifted food prices.
On a month-to-month basis, consumer prices were roughly flat from August, Tuesday's data showed.
Taiwan's central bank has kept interest rates unchanged for the past nine quarters, as artificial-intelligence demand fueled export-led growth while inflation remained moderate.
However, the island's recent inflation uptick has put investors on alert ahead of the Central Bank of the Republic of China's policy decision next Thursday.
ING economists expect a rate increase this month, while DBS economists see December as the more likely window.
Rising oil prices and surging Treasury yields have raised the odds that the Federal Reserve will increase interest rates at its meeting next week.
A Fed rate increase could add pressure on Taiwan's central bank to tighten monetary policy, economists said.
